                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> was right in the eyes of, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> pleased Absalom well, and all the Elders of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> what is in his mouth.</ns0:note> what he saith <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">A wonderful Effect of Divine Providence, blinding his Mind, and Influencing his Heart, that he could not rest in <ns0:hi>Ahitophel</ns0:hi>'s Counsel, though it was so evidently Wise, and Good, and approved by the general consent of his whole Party; and that he should desire <ns0:hi>Hushai</ns0:hi>'s Advice, though neither his Repuation for Wisdom was equal to <ns0:hi>Ahitophels,</ns0:hi> nor had he yet given any one proof of his Fidelity to <ns0:hi>Absa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lom,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Ahitophel</ns0:hi> had done; nor was he so fixed by his In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terest to him, as <ns0:hi>Ahitophel</ns0:hi> was; and though there wanted not just Cause to suspect him, and his Counsel too. But there is no contending with that God who can Arm a Man against himself, and Destroy him by his own Mistakes and Passions, without any other help.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: Shall we do <ns0:hi>after</ns0:hi> his <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> Word.</ns0:note> saying? if not, speak thou.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 And Hushai said unto Absalom, The coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel that Ahithophel hath <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selled.</ns0:note> given, <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> not good at this time <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Though at other times he generally gives most wise and admirable Counsel; yet, as he is a man, he seems now to be under a mistake, and not sufficiently to consider all the present Circumstances of this Business.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 For (said Hushai) thou knowest thy father and his men, that they <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> mighty men <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Of approved Courage and Strength, therefore not so soon vanquished as <ns0:hi>Ahitophel</ns0:hi> supposeth.</ns0:note>, and they <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>H<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>b.</ns0:hi> bitter of soul.</ns0:note> chafed in their minds <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>bitter of soul,</ns0:hi> Inflamed with Rage; Desperate, and therefore re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />solved to sell their Lives at a dear rate.</ns0:note>, as <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Hos. 13. 8.</ns0:note> a bear robbed of her whelps in the field <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>bitter of soul,</ns0:hi> Inflamed with Rage; Desperate, and therefore re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />solved to sell their Lives at a dear rate.</ns0:note>: and thy father <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> a man of war <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">A wise Prince and General; who knowing of what Importance it is to secure his own Person, and that your great Design is against his Life; will doubtless use extraordinary care to keep out of your reach, which he may easily do.</ns0:note>, and will not lodge with the people.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some <ns0:hi>other</ns0:hi> place <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Having been oft accustomed to that course, and well ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quainted with all hiding-places from <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi>'s time. In one of them, unknown to us, he will lurk with some of his chosen men, and lie in Ambush for us; and, when they see a fit op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />portunity, they will suddenly come forth and surprize some of our men, when they least expect it, and fall upon them with great fury, and probably will at first put them to flight.</ns0:note>: and it will come to pass, when some of them <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">To wit, of <ns0:hi>Absalom</ns0:hi>'s men sent against <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> be <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> fallen.</ns0:note> overthrown at the first <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Imply<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, that their good success at first would mightily animate <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s men to proceed vigorously in the fight, and intimi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />date <ns0:hi>Absalom</ns0:hi>'s Army, and consequently would be both a presage and an occasion of their total defeat.</ns0:note>, that whosoever heareth it, will say <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">They who first hear these ill tidings will propagate it, and strike terror with it into the rest of the Army.</ns0:note>, There is a slaughter among the people that followeth Ab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>alom.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:262" />10 And he also <ns0:hi>that is</ns0:hi> valiant, whose heart <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael knoweth that thy father <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> a mighty man, and <ns0:hi>they</ns0:hi> which <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> with him <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> valiant men <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The known fame of the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> valour of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> and his followers will easily gain credit to that report, and strike the stourest of our men with dread, even <ns0:hi>Ahitophel</ns0:hi> himself, if he should go with them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 Therefore I counsel, that all Israel be gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rally gathered unto thee <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">His pretence was, that they might have a far greater Army, and make sure, though slow work: his design was to gain <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> more time, that he might increase his Army, and make better provisions for the Battel; and that the pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent heat of the people might be cooled, and they might at last bethink themselves of their duty to <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and return to their former Allegiance.</ns0:note>, from Dan even to Beer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sheba, as the sand that <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> by the sea for multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude, and <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> that thy face, or, presence go, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> that thou go to battel in thine own person <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">For thy presence will put more Life and Courage into all thy Soldiers, who will be ambitious to shew their utmost Skill and Courage in defending thy Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son and Cause, when they know that all their Actions are observed by him who hath the distribution of rewards and punishments in his hands. So mayest thou also give counsel as occasion offers, and encourage thy men to kill <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> which otherwise they may possibly be afraid to do. Besides, the glory of the Victory will be wholly thine, which now <ns0:hi>Ahitophel</ns0:hi> seeks to get to himself.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Plenteously, suddenly, irresistibly, and on all sides; for so the Dew falls.</ns0:note>: and of him, and of all the men that <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> with him, there shall not be left so much as one.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Not that they should do so, or that it was the Custom to do so; but it is an Hyperbolical and Thrasonical expression, suited to the vain-glorious temper of this insolent young man; and therefore most likely to prevail with him: imply<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, that they would do so if they could not discover and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroy him another way: or, that they should be enough to do so, if there were occasion.</ns0:note>, and we will draw it into the river <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Adjoyning to the City; it being usual to build Cities near some River, both for defence, and for other accommodations.</ns0:note>, until there be not one small stone sound there.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And Absalom and all the men of Israel said <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Being infatuated by a Divine power, and given up to believe lyes and mistakes.</ns0:note>, The counsel of Hushai the Archite <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> better than the counsel of Ahithophel: for the LORD had <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded.</ns0:note> appointed to defeat the good counsel <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">So it was, politically consider<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed; being the wisest and most effectual course to accom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plish <ns0:hi>Absalom</ns0:hi>'s end.</ns0:note> of Ahitho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil upon Absalom.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 ¶ Then said Hushai unto Zadok, and to Abia<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithopel coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel Absalom and the elders of Israel: and thus and thus have I counselled.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 Now therefore send quickly, and tell Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Lest the Kings and peoples minds change, and <ns0:hi>A<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>ito<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phel</ns0:hi> by his deep wit and great interest, persuade the King to follow his former advice, and to pursue you speedily.</ns0:note>, but speedily pass over, lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> with him.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz staied by En<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rogel <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>the Fullers well.</ns0:hi> A place near <ns0:hi>Ierusalem, Ios.</ns0:hi> 15. 7. and 18. 16.</ns0:note>: (for they might not be seen to come into the city) and a wench <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Pretending to go thither to wash some Cloathes.</ns0:note> went and told them: and they went and told king David.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 Nevertheless, a lad saw them <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Who knew them to be favourers of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />served them to wait there upon design, and to gain intelli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gence, and possibly saw the Wench speaking privately to them.</ns0:note>, and told Ab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salom, but they went both of them away quick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Suspecting by this Lads observation and carriage, that they were discovered.</ns0:note>, and came to a mans house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court, whither they went down <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Either to some hole in the side of the Pit: or, to the bottom of the Pit, it being then dry, as Pits often were in those hot Countries. And this being in so open a place, they concluded none would imagine them to be hid there. And besides, they relied upon Gods good Providence, which they knew watched over <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and them for his sake.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And the woman took and spread a covering over the wells mouth, and spread ground corn thereon <ns0:note place="bottom">Under pretence of drying it by the Sun: which shews it was Summer-time.</ns0:note>, and the thing was not known.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 And when Absaloms servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Over <ns0:hi>Iordan.</ns0:hi> This was a manifest lye; but because it was spoken for no hurt, but good onely, many persons in those times conceived such lies to be lawful. Compare <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 1. 19. <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 2. 4, 5. But although God was pleased to over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />look and pardon the sin, and graciously to reward the good intention which accompanied them; yet it is certain that all kinds of lyes are moral Evils, and condemned by plain Scri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ptures, and that <ns0:hi>we must not do evil that good may come,</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>tell a lye for Gods glory,</ns0:hi> Rom. 3. 7, 8.</ns0:note>. And when they had sought, and could not find <ns0:hi>them,</ns0:hi> they re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turned to Jerusalem.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And it came to pass, after they were depart<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hithophel counselled against you.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 Then David arose, and all the people that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> with him, and they passed over Jordan <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Either at the Ford, or in Boats.</ns0:note>: by the morning-light, there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 ¶ And when Ahithophel saw that his coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel was not <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> done.</ns0:note> followed, he sadled <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> asse, and arose, and gate him home to his house, to his city, and <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> gare charge con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning his house.</ns0:note> put his houshold in order <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Disposed of his Estate by Will. Compare <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 38. 1.</ns0:note>, and hanged himself <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Partly, because he could not indure to outlive his disgrace, and the rejection of his Counsel: and partly, because he foresaw by this means <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> would gain time and strength, and in all probability be Victorious, and then the storm would fall most heavily upon his head, as the main Author and Pillar of the Rebellion, and the contriver of those two pernicious Counsels above mentioned.</ns0:note>, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 Then David came to Mahanaim <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">A place in the Countrey of <ns0:hi>Gilead,</ns0:hi> bordering upon the Land of the <ns0:hi>Ammonites, v.</ns0:hi> 27. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 32. 2. and 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 2. 8.</ns0:note>: and Ab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salom passed over Jordan <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Not speedily, but when <ns0:hi>all the men of Israel</ns0:hi> were gathered together according to <ns0:hi>Hushai</ns0:hi>'s counsel, who are said to be <ns0:hi>with him</ns0:hi> here, as it follows.</ns0:note>, and all the men of Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael with him.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:262" />25 ¶ And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> a mans son whose name <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> Ithra, an Israelite <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Obj.</ns0:hi> He was an <ns0:hi>Ishmaelite,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 2. 17. <ns0:hi>Ans.</ns0:hi> Not <ns0:hi>Amasa;</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>Ithra,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Iether, Amasa</ns0:hi>'s Father, is there so cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led, because he was such, either by his Birth from such Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rents, or by his long habitation among them, or for some o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther reason now unknown. Compare 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 15. 18. And <ns0:hi>Amasa</ns0:hi> is here called an <ns0:hi>Israelite,</ns0:hi> either, because he was a Proselyte: or, in opposition to <ns0:hi>Ioab,</ns0:hi> who was of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Amasa</ns0:hi> was of one of the ten Tribes: or rather, to intimate, that although he or his Parents were called <ns0:hi>Ishmae<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lites</ns0:hi> for some reason, yet as to their extraction they were indeed <ns0:hi>Israelites.</ns0:hi> Which if <ns0:hi>Amasa</ns0:hi> had not been, it is not probable that he could have had so powerful an influence upon the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> as he had, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 19. 14.</ns0:note>, that went in to Abigail <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Lay with her, whether being first Married to her, or not, is un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />certain.</ns0:note> the daughter of Nahash <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Nahash</ns0:hi> is either another name of <ns0:hi>Iesse:</ns0:hi> or ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, the name of <ns0:hi>Iesse</ns0:hi>'s Wife, by whom he had this <ns0:hi>Abi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gail,</ns0:hi> as he had <ns0:hi>Zeruiah</ns0:hi> by another Wife; so they were si<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sters by the Father, but not by the Mother; and <ns0:hi>Nahash</ns0:hi> is here named to signify so much.</ns0:note>, sister to Zeruiah, Joabs mother.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 So Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 ¶ And it came to pass when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Who, as it may seem, disliked and disowned that bar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />barous action to the Embassadors; and therefore, when the rest were destroyed, was left King or Governor of the residue of the <ns0:hi>Ammonites.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9. 4.</ns0:note> Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">See above <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9. 4.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 19. 31. 1 King. 2. 7.</ns0:note> Barzillai the Gileadite, of Rogelim,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 Brought beds, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> cups.</ns0:note> basins <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> All sorts <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>of Houshold-stuff, as well as other pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ons, all which <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> now wanted.</ns0:note>, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parch<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:hi>corn,</ns0:hi> and beans, and lentiles, and parched <ns0:hi>pulse,</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="29">29 And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine for David, and for the people that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> with him, to eat: for they said, The people <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> hungry, and weary, and thirsty in the wilder<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Having been <ns0:hi>in the wilderness.</ns0:hi> Which is an easie and common Ellipsis. Or, <ns0:hi>because of</ns0:hi> (so the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> Par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticle <ns0:hi>hath</ns0:hi> is oft used) <ns0:hi>the Wilderness,</ns0:hi> which they have passed thorough, in which provisions are very scarce.</ns0:note>
